title: Cloud-Vessel Balloon Festival
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk, Lu Chuan（Lu Chuan, a forty-year-old hot-air-balloon captain: goggles on, khaki flight jacket, walkie-talkie at his belt, focused expression） walks onto the inflation lawn（Inflation lawn: open green turf, wear-resistant canvas at center, colorful balloons rising in the distance） and first checks the seams of the red-and-white striped main envelope（A red-and-white striped main envelope, swollen like a giant egg; wicker basket below, burner nozzle gleaming）.
Along the lawn edge stands a row of five signal flags（A row of five signal flags in bases along the lawn edge, red, yellow, and blue alternating）; Lu Chuan turns each one to face the wind.
Two fog bells（Two fog bells hanging under the control-tower eaves, low-toned when fog rolls in） hang under the control-tower eaves; Lu Chuan reaches up and lets them ring softly.
Lu Chuan circles the basket, checking the wicker for cracks.
Lu Chuan climbs the viewing berm and gazes at the darkening sky.
The main envelope billows gently in the evening breeze; Lu Chuan feels the fabric's temperature.
Lu Chuan sits on a folding chair at the lawn edge for a brief rest.
Lu Chuan opens the flight logbook（A leather-bound flight logbook recording wind direction, temperature, and passenger names） and notes the day's wind speed and dew point.
Lu Chuan draws a wind-direction arrow in the flight logbook.
Lu Chuan closes the flight logbook and tucks it into the basket side pocket.
The main envelope's top vent valve opens and closes slightly; Lu Chuan nods.
Lu Chuan wipes dew from the flight logbook cover with a dry cloth.

At dawn on the viewing berm（Viewing berm: a tan slope overlooking the whole lawn, windsock planted on top）, Lu Chuan greets young apprentice Afan（Young ground-crew apprentice Afan, fourteen or fifteen, indigo headscarf, orange vest, bright stubborn eyes） arriving in the ground-crew pickup（A tan ground-crew pickup with gas cylinders and sandbags in the bed, doors stenciled 'Cloud-Vessel-07'）.
Afan jumps down from the pickup and tightens the gas-cylinder valve cap.
Lu Chuan points to three hemp sandbags（Three hemp sandbags strung on blue cord and pressed to the basket rim, cloud patterns on the bags） at the basket rim and teaches Afan to read the ballast marks.
Afan crouches in the berm grass, watching the windsock swing with curiosity.
Lu Chuan explains emergency deflation steps; Afan nods earnestly.
Afan looks back at the tan ground-crew pickup, eyes full of longing.
Lu Chuan has Afan practice holding the basket rope steady.

In the bustling market tent quarter（Market tent quarter: colored canopies in a row, hot drinks and postcards for sale, noisy crowd）, Ayi（Youth Ayi, face extremely like Afan's, ivory silk scarf, same orange vest, bold expression） with an ivory silk scarf looks up from behind a hot-drink stall.
Ayi picks balloon-pattern postcards at a stall, scarf fluttering.
Ayi haggles with the vendor, expression bold.
Ayi carries a paper bag through the tent crowd.
Ayi pauses under colored awnings and glances back at the inflation lawn.
On the viewing berm, Afan and Ayi stand side by side—one with an indigo headscarf, one with an ivory silk scarf.
Afan hands sandbags to Ayi; the two check the weight together.
Ayi straightens Afan's indigo headscarf; the two walk slowly along the berm.
Afan and Ayi part at the berm crest, one heading for the lawn, one for the market.
Evening wind passes; their similar orange vests cross and separate in the berm shadows.
Months later at night, Lu Chuan keeps watch alone on the inflation lawn.
Lu Chuan opens the flight logbook（The same flight logbook soaked by a downpour: cover wrinkled, ink blurred） and finds a storm has soaked the cover wrinkled.
Lu Chuan wipes condensation from the main envelope fabric.
Lu Chuan looks toward the dark viewing berm.
The main envelope sways gently in the night wind; Lu Chuan grips the basket rope.
Lu Chuan slips blotting paper into the rain-stained flight logbook and presses it under an atlas.
During the rainy season, Lu Chuan wipes and oils damp gas-cylinder valves on the inflation lawn.
Lu Chuan brushes carbon buildup from the burner nozzle.
At dawn, Lu Chuan checks the competition balloon roster on the viewing berm.
Lu Chuan hangs a rain poncho on the flagpole and listens to the windsock snap.
In midsummer, Lu Chuan stretches shade netting over the inflation lawn to protect the main envelope.
Lu Chuan checks whether the basket floor screws are loose.
As autumn wind rises, Lu Chuan furls extra signal flags so they won't blow over.
Lu Chuan tries a new route code on a blank page of the flight logbook.
On a frosty night, Lu Chuan lights camp lanterns and checks flashlight batteries.
Lu Chuan wraps gas cylinders in blankets to prevent overnight condensation.
On a snowy day, Lu Chuan sweeps thin snow from the old airport portico steps.
Lu Chuan breathes on his hands and retightens the sandbags' blue cords.
In early spring, Lu Chuan trims shrubs along the berm to expose the windsock.
Lu Chuan mends each corner of the five signal flags.
Lu Chuan posts a new launch-order sheet on the control-tower wall.
Around the Dragon Boat festival, Lu Chuan smokes out mosquitoes in the tent quarter with mugwort.
Lu Chuan retraces the cloud patterns printed on the sandbags.
Lu Chuan paces the berm alone, silently reciting emergency commands.
After the rain stops, Lu Chuan pushes aside a tent flap and listens to water dripping into a tin bucket.
Lu Chuan swaps out worn gloves for new ones.
Another dusk, Lu Chuan sits beside the main envelope listening to the campfire crackle.
Lu Chuan gets up at night to refuel the camp heater.
Lu Chuan waxes newly arrived basket ropes against wear.
Lu Chuan polishes the 'Cloud-Vessel Flight' lintel on the old airport portico.
Lu Chuan checks the pickup bed for cracks.
Lu Chuan marks no-fly zones on the aviation chart.
Lu Chuan wrings out a mud-stained rag and hangs it on the flagpole.
On a full-moon night, Lu Chuan looks down from the berm; the main envelope gleams silver.
Lu Chuan aligns the flag bases so the signal flags face the same way.
Lu Chuan writes a new season's festival notes on the flight logbook flyleaf.
Lu Chuan polishes the two fog bells.
Lu Chuan keeps registering passengers while market hand-drums sound in the distance.
Lu Chuan glues a cracked folding chair back together.
Lu Chuan stacks old envelope fabric awaiting repair in a lawn corner.
Lu Chuan latches the toolbox shut against overnight damp.
Another Qingming, Lu Chuan places a bunch of wildflowers on the old airport portico.
Lu Chuan rolls the aviation chart into a tube and binds it with a rubber band.
Lu Chuan tests the fog bells' low tone; the sound carries long.
Lu Chuan sits silently on the inflation lawn, listening to wind over the main envelope for a long while.
Lu Chuan cuts worn indigo cloth into rag stock.
Lu Chuan sharpens the burner ignition needle.
At daybreak, Lu Chuan patrols the viewing berm; the tan ground-crew pickup is parked below.
Lu Chuan crouches to check how deep mud is on the pickup tires.
Lu Chuan walks to the basket rim; the same three hemp sandbags still hang on blue cord.
A white camper van（A white camper van, long-bodied, no 'Cloud-Vessel-07' marking—unlike the tan pickup） passes the berm—long-bodied, not a Cloud-Vessel pickup.
Lu Chuan stands on the berm and records the windsock angle.
Lu Chuan hangs wet canvas on a wooden rack on the berm.
Lu Chuan brushes grass from his jacket and looks back at the lawn lights.
After Grain Rain, Lu Chuan teaches new ground crew to read windsock angles on the berm.
Lu Chuan folds the dried rain poncho back into the pickup toolbox.
In summer heat, Lu Chuan presses a damp cloth to gas-cylinder shells to cool them.
Lu Chuan checks the pickup bed and moves damp sandbags to the upper layer.
On an autumn night, Lu Chuan mends loose pages of the flight logbook under camp lights.
Lu Chuan rotates the five signal flags through the wash.
At first snow, Lu Chuan clears a narrow path across the old airport portico threshold.
Lu Chuan refolds the spare auxiliary envelope and packs it into a crate.
Lu Chuan keeps revising the flight plan as fog bells ring softly.
Lu Chuan opens the tent door and lets a cross-breeze carry damp away.
Lu Chuan hangs rain canvas under the old airport portico.
Lu Chuan stows a burned ignition needle in a tin box.
Lu Chuan dreams the envelope is leaking, wakes, and writes it in the flight logbook.
Lu Chuan rinses mud spots from the flag bases with clean water.
Lu Chuan wipes and re-nails the launch-order sheet.
Lu Chuan pulls weeds from cracks in the berm stone.
Lu Chuan reseats signal flags in their bases; numbered tabs somewhat faded.
Before lights-out, Lu Chuan takes one last look at main envelope seams.
Lu Chuan folds an indigo headscarf an apprentice left on the lawn.
Lu Chuan hears the market closing horn and gets up to lock the gate.
Lu Chuan dries gloves by the campfire.
Lu Chuan moves the fog bells aside to show the freshly repaired tower eaves.
Lu Chuan hangs wind-test streamers on the flagpole.
Lu Chuan sketches a wind-speed comparison on the last page of the flight logbook.
Lu Chuan murmurs tomorrow's launch window and steps out of the old airport portico.
Lu Chuan pushes the pickup against the wall to clear inflation space.
Lu Chuan hears distant roosters and blows out the camp lanterns.
Another rainy night, Lu Chuan keeps watch over the main envelope until dawn.
A storm bursts; on the inflation lawn the main envelope shakes violently.
Lightning lights the burner nozzle; the basket lurches hard.

A burst of uncontrolled flame burns through the main envelope（The same main envelope burned through by flame: striped fabric collapsed and leaking, basket tilted）; the breach leaks and the fabric collapses.
On the viewing berm, the tan ground-crew pickup skids in a mudslide.
The ground-crew pickup（The ground-crew pickup has plunged off the viewing berm: hood crumpled, bed twisted—an unmovable wreck） plunges off the berm; hood crumpled, bed twisted, utterly wrecked.
Lu Chuan lunges for the basket and presses hard on the cracking main envelope patch.
Ground crew arrive with lanterns; the lawn is mud and water.
The next day, Lu Chuan stands on the inflation lawn, staring at the breached main envelope.
Lu Chuan runs a finger along the scorched fabric edge, expression dark.
Lu Chuan notes the date the ground-crew pickup fell off the berm in a blank page of the flight logbook.
A dispatch photo of the ground-crew pickup still hangs on the control-tower wall; Lu Chuan stares a long time.
Lu Chuan takes one of the row of five signal flags from its base and realigns it to the wind.
The damaged main envelope still lies half-deflated on the canvas.
Lu Chuan sets muddy boots at the lawn edge to drain.
Weeks later, Lu Chuan brings in a patch specialist to repair the main envelope.

Lu Chuan drags a spare auxiliary envelope（A spare auxiliary envelope, smaller, solid blue without stripes—looks like the main envelope but cannot carry passengers） from storage to compare—it is smaller, solid blue, no stripes.
The patch specialist sews the breach tight with heavy-duty thread.
The last tear is sewn shut; the main envelope（The main envelope patched with heavy-duty thread and reinflated; the repair patch clearly visible） reinflates and swells again.
The repaired main envelope gleams in morning light; Lu Chuan looks at the patch with relief.
Lu Chuan relights the burner nozzle and test-lifts one meter.
Photographer Lao Jin（Photographer Lao Jin, long telephoto lens, wide-brim hat, build near Lu Chuan's but taller and thinner） arrives on the berm, wide-brim hat and long lens, build near Lu Chuan's.
The ATC coordinator（A lean air-traffic coordinator, headset on, hi-vis vest, build somewhat like Lu Chuan's but stiffer） arrives too, hi-vis vest and headset, standing beside Lu Chuan to talk.
The coordinator points at the white camper van and asks whether it belongs to the Cloud-Vessel team.
The coordinator leaves; Lu Chuan remains alone on the viewing berm.
Lao Jin folds his tripod and bows farewell.
At the market comes Xiaohe（Market girl Xiaohe, light-brown headscarf, at a glance somewhat like young Afan, shy eyes） with a light-brown headscarf—a glance makes her look like young Afan.
Xiaohe tries arranging postcards; Lu Chuan shakes his head—she is not Afan after all.
Xiaohe lowers her eyes shyly and reties her ribbon.

Years later at dusk, wounded Lu Chuan（The same Lu Chuan: jacket torn, forehead wounded, leaning on a trekking pole as he walks slowly, goggles still hanging on his chest） stands on his trekking pole at the old airport portico（Old airport portico: gray-brick arcade, lintel carved 'Cloud-Vessel Flight', moss on the steps）.
Lu Chuan looks up at the 'Cloud-Vessel Flight' lintel, gaze far away.
The two fog bells from the tower have been moved to the portico for a test ring; Lu Chuan stops to listen.
Lu Chuan presses his palm to the cool gray-brick arch, as if saying goodbye.
Evening wind lifts the hem of his torn jacket.
By day, adult Afan（Afan in his twenties, still in an indigo headscarf and orange vest, tall and steady） returns along the ramp and hurries toward the old airport portico.
Afan reunites with Lu Chuan on his trekking pole under the portico; the two embrace.
Beside a bamboo couch in the lounge, Afan holds Lu Chuan's hand.

Lu Chuan（Lu Chuan has stepped down; only his old flight jacket and goggles remain on the inflation lawn—he himself no longer appears）'s breath fades; he finally closes his eyes and steps down from duty.
Afan folds Lu Chuan's flight jacket and sets it by the pillow.
Lu Chuan's goggles still hang behind the portico; Afan reaches out and touches them gently.
On a portico pillar, Afan stands before the newly nailed memorial brass plaque（A brass memorial plaque nailed to a portico pillar, engraved with Lu Chuan's name and first-flight year）.
Afan's fingertips trace Lu Chuan's name engraved on the memorial brass plaque.
Afan places a bunch of wildflowers below the memorial brass plaque.
Remade Ayi（Remade Ayi still wears the ivory silk scarf, expression deeper and quieter） hurries from the market and embraces Afan tightly under the portico.
Afan and Ayi stand side by side under the portico—one calm-eyed, one deep in expression.
The two look at each other in silence, studying similar faces.
Ayi tightens her ivory silk scarf; Afan still wears the indigo headscarf.
The frame returns to years ago—the boy holding the basket rope steady on the berm appears again.
The opening moment returns—on the lawn, a red-and-white striped main envelope swells and rises for the first time.
Flash back to the market that year—the orange-vest figure with an ivory silk scarf flashes past.
Before the eyes rises again the row of five colored flags along the lawn edge.
The tan slope from first sight returns, windsock swinging as before.
The image returns of the two old bells ringing softly under the control-tower eaves.
Afan opens the rain-stained flight logbook again and walks onto the inflation lawn.
At the basket rim, the same three hemp sandbags still hang on blue cord.
Afan takes over the patched main envelope and relights the burner nozzle.
Fresh green pushes through cracks in the berm grass.
Afan tightens his indigo headscarf; the balloon rises again.
